issues.description: The problem statement requires implementing a function named `print_newline` (problem_statement.md: line 22), but the solution repository defines a function labeled `print_nl` (solution_repository/helloWorld.asm: lines 6-7) and the template repository does not provide a `print_newline` stub. This name/signature mismatch means students following the problem text (or automated checks expecting `print_newline`) will not find the corresponding implementation in the solution and may be confused about the correct symbol to implement or call. It also risks automated grading or example code using a different name than the specification.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the function name consistent across artifacts. Rename the solution label `print_nl` to `print_newline` (and, if needed, add a corresponding stub in the template repository) so the solution, template, and problem statement all reference the same function name. Alternatively, update the problem statement to request `print_nl` if that name is intended. Ensure the function is declared/placed where students expect to find and call it (or clearly document that they should create it).

issues.description: The problem statement explicitly asks students to implement a function named `print_newline`, but the solution repository defines a label `print_nl` instead and the template repository does not provide a `print_newline` stub. This naming mismatch (print_newline vs print_nl) creates a mapping barrier: students following the problem will implement `print_newline` while the reference solution uses a differently named symbol, causing confusion about the expected identifier.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the identifier consistent across artifacts. Recommended: rename the solution label `print_nl` to `print_newline` (and update any internal comments) and add a `print_newline:` stub in the template file so students have the exact symbol the problem requests. Alternatively, if `print_nl` is preferred, change the problem text to request `print_nl` instead — but keep names identical across problem, template, and solution.
